A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures and appendices. Sections 1–7, Figures 1–6 and Algorithm 1 can be matched reliably, including material retained or relocated around v4's new appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports theorems, proofs and analytically worked network examples, including its appendices. It reports no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v4 retains the theoretical focus. Its new Appendices I–J contain mathematical statements and proofs, and no original empirical evaluation is reported elsewhere.

M1.justification: The P_r and M_k relaxations, input-copying network transformation and polytope-partitioning Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Section 2.3 revises the motivation for M_k without changing its procedure; the new network constructions serve as theoretical witnesses.

E1.justification: Neither version uses training or evaluation datasets. The max-function example already uses [0,1]^d in v3; v4 makes that domain explicit in surrounding descriptions. The activation-function extensions are theoretical, not new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. Triangle, k-ReLU, IBP and DeepPoly remain in the analytical comparisons. Appendix H's new runtime discussion concerns the already discussed DeepPoly method.

E3.justification: No experimental splits, preprocessing, training budgets or testing procedures are introduced or revised. Appendix I defines relative bounding error for mathematical theorems, not as a newly applied empirical evaluation metric.

E4.justification: The existing zero-function, max-function and partitioning examples are retained. No ablations, robustness tests or empirical error analyses are added. Appendix H adds a runtime interpretation of the existing example, while Appendices I–J supply theoretical arguments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical uncertainty estimates. Mathematical approximation-error bounds are not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The worked-example values remain unchanged: Section 5.1 reports an exact upper bound of 1 for M_1 versus 1.5 for k-ReLU, and Appendix H retains 1 versus 2^(d−1) partitions. No empirical result entries change; the additions concern theoretical guarantees and complexity arguments.

T1.justification: v4 adds Theorems I.1–I.2 on unbounded relative bounding error and Lemma J.1, Proposition J.2 and Theorems J.3–J.4 formalizing the non-polynomial activation extension only sketched in v3 Section 4. Appendix H adds runtime-scaling reasoning, while Sections 2.2 and E.3 explicitly state nonempty-input and unequal-interval-endpoint assumptions. These substantially expand the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The introductory max-function contribution now explicitly specifies [0,1]^d instead of R^d, matching the domain already used in v3's demonstration. The abstract and conclusion retain the universal convex barrier and completeness-through-transformation-or-partitioning claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds 'Result Contexts', spelling out the negative results' quantifiers and limiting positive results to finite ReLU networks. Appendix A explicitly distinguishes deterministic from probabilistic certification. Section 5.2 and Appendix H extend the existing partition-count discussion to a polynomial-versus-exponential runtime claim for P_1 and BaB with DeepPoly.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Appendix D's implementation caveats are retained. No code or data access information, executable implementation, hyperparameters, hardware details or measured runtimes are added. Appendix H discusses asymptotic complexity only.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a short distinction from probabilistic certification and six references: Cohen et al. (2019), Lécuyer et al. (2019), Salman et al. (2020), Carlini et al. (2023), and Sun et al. (2025a,b). The broader positioning is retained; several other bibliography changes update existing works' publication details.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized language and terminology edits, adds discussion subheadings and acknowledgments, and updates author and publication information. New Appendices I–J precede the unchanged LLM disclosure, moved from Appendix I to K. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: All six figures and Algorithm 1 are retained, with no new tables. Figure 3 is enlarged, Figure 6's solid separator becomes dashed, and Figure 4's caption typo is corrected. Conference headers and text reflow produce limited placement and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies scope and supplies formal arguments for the non-polynomial extension that v3 only sketched. However, the new Theorem I.1 proof asserts that h(x)=x_2(x_2+x_1−1) vanishes on f_1(X), although its displayed set contains (0,2), where h=2. The subsequent output-range bound therefore does not follow as printed, and Theorem I.2 reuses it. Useful clarification and expanded proof detail coexist with a defect in a principal new theoretical addition, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
